answers.core: Transforming patterns in this way is already a feature of the editor interface. It's confusing to have a feature be significantly less useful when accessed in code, and gives a bad impression of the engine overall, especially for the pattern system which already has its fair share of pain points.
answers.workaround:
I've been mapping out a system to iterate through the patterns at runtime and create new, transformed copies of them as needed. It will work, but it's going to be _way_ more than a few lines, and doing all of this in GDScript seems inefficient, especially since I'm targeting HTML.

Discussing this issue on the Discord, I immediately ran into another user who ran into the same issue. They ended up making a series of duplicate rotated/flipped patterns, then manually plugging the index of every single one into a series of arrays, which needs to be manually adjusted any time a pattern gets removed. This limitation causes a lot of headache for people trying to make use of the Pattern system, and it drives them to absurd workarounds if they don't have the programming skills to build a proper workaround, which doesn't make sense for an engine that prioritizes accessibility.

title: Expose TileMapPattern flip/transpose functionality (as seen in the editor) to TileMapLayer.set_pattern()
